extends.label: Extends
extends.help: A base profile: this profile inherits its interfaces, data points and files and lists only what it adds or changes.
extends.chainHelp: Inherited items show where they come from. Change one to override it here, or mark it as not present.

unused: Changes to items the base no longer has are ignored: {{items}}

aliases.label: Known as
aliases.help: Names tools commonly use for this data point, such as a gateway's variable names. Imports of data collections match them.

additions.title: Added on this asset
additions.help: Data points and interfaces of this asset alone. They count as delivered like the profile's data points.

collections.title: Data collections
collections.help: What collectors – gateways, ETL jobs – read from this asset: how often, under which name, where they load it, and the data point each value is.

totals.mapped: items mapped to a data point

collections.emptyText: Import a collector's configuration – a gateway's JSON, a table, a connector export or a Node-RED flow – to document what it reads.
collections.whoCanAct: Whoever manages this site can import data collections.
collections.writesTitle: This collector may change the machine
collections.writesText: Its access patterns allow writing, creating or deleting at these addresses.
collections.duplicate: The same data point as item {{items}}
collections.unknownAddress: No data point of this asset has this address

formats.gateway_json: Gateway JSON – datasets of data points

collections.mapTitle: Map the item to a data point
collections.idHelp: Letters, digits, ".", "_" and "-", starting with a letter, digit or "_"
collections.idTaken: The asset has a data point with this id already
collections.noAssignment: The asset has no assignment yet: assign a device profile first
collections.addTitle: Add the address as a data point of this asset
collections.addHelp: The asset gets a data point of its own at this address; the collector's name becomes its known-as name.
collections.stale: A data point the asset no longer has
collections.noneRead: No data collection reads this data point.

import.title: Import data collections
import.help: Choose the collector and its configuration files. The preview suggests a data point for every item; you confirm or change them before anything is written.
import.replace: Remove this collector's collections that the files no longer have
import.previewFormatText: This importer is built from public examples and may still change. Check the result.
import.aliasProfile: As a known-as name of the data point
import.recordAddress: Record this address as the asset's address of the data point
import.recordAddressOther: Record this address as the asset's address (now {{address}})
import.summary: {{mapped}} items mapped, {{raw}} raw; {{addresses}} addresses recorded, {{aliases}} names remembered, {{added}} data points added.
import.done: Imported: {{added}} collections added, {{changed}} changed, {{removed}} removed; {{mapped}} items mapped, {{raw}} raw.

collections.name: Name
collections.nameTaken: The asset has a collection with this name already

template.label: Template – only for other profiles to extend
template.help: A template is no device of its own: no asset can have it. Profiles that extend it can (a template is not inherited).
template.badgeHelp: Only for other profiles to extend – no asset can have this profile.

units.label: Expected units
units.help: The unit the computation expects per data point. Left empty: the unit the data point has in the profile. An asset that delivers another unit is flagged.
units.line: {{point}}: expects {{expected}}, delivers {{actual}} – not convertible by a factor
units.lineConvertible: {{point}}: expects {{expected}}, delivers {{actual}} – convertible by a factor

potential.readyHelp: A data collection of the asset maps every data point the KPI reads: a job can start.
potential.collectHelp: The device delivers every input, but no data collection of the asset maps all of them yet.

extract.title: Extract a base profile
extract.help: The data points that two or more profiles share become a new base profile that each of them extends. Ids that differ are renamed to the base’s (the old id still leads there; assets, KPI definitions and data collections follow), fields that differ stay as each profile’s overrides – no asset changes.
extract.profilesHelp: Two or more, none that extends another already
extract.leadingHelp: The base takes the name, data type, unit and description of its data points
extract.pointsHelp: Suggested by the same id, a known-as name and the name (same unit preferred). Change a match where it is wrong; a data point that one profile lacks cannot be shared.
extract.name: Name of the base profile
extract.templateHelp: On: no asset can have the base – only the profiles that extend it.
extract.refusedPoints_one: {{count}} data point cannot go into the base – leave it out or change the profiles first.
extract.refusedPoints_other: {{count}} data points cannot go into the base – leave them out or change the profiles first.
extract.ok: The base gets {{points}} data points on {{interfaces}} interfaces. Every asset’s data points stay as they are.
extract.summary: {{renames}} ids renamed · {{overrides}} data points differ from the base · keeps {{interfaces}} own interfaces and {{points}} own data points · {{assets}} assets (unchanged)

problems.protocol: {{point}} of {{profile}} is on a {{protocol}} interface, in the leading profile on {{leading}} – a base holds one protocol per interface.
problems.group: {{point}} of {{profile}} is in group “{{group}}”, in the leading profile in “{{leading}}” – rename the group first.
problems.interface: {{point}} of {{profile}} is on interface {{interface}}, which other shared data points place elsewhere.
problems.id_taken: {{point}} of {{profile}} cannot get the id {{id}}: it is taken.
problems.has_base: {{profile}} extends {{base}} already – only profiles without a base can get a new one.
problems.not_enough: Choose two or more device profiles.
problems.leading: The leading profile is one of the chosen profiles.
problems.no_points: Choose at least one data point every profile can share.
problems.base_taken: A device profile with the id {{id}} exists already.
problems.rules: The result breaks a rule of device profiles: {{message}}

extract.interfacesHelp: Each profile’s interface that holds the shared data points gets this id. Where their protocols differ, the base’s interface has the protocol “other” and no addresses – each profile keeps its protocol and addresses.

anyOf.profilesHelp: Empty: whatever profile the asset has. Several: any of them – an asset whose profile is (or extends) one of them delivers the input. The data points are the first profile’s.
anyOf.mapping: Data points in the other profiles
anyOf.mappingHelp: Per profile, its data point for each input – suggested by the same id, a known-as name, the name and the unit. Change a suggestion where it is wrong.
anyOf.missing: No such data point – choose one

rollUp.label: Roll up from parts
rollUp.help: An asset counts as able to have the KPI when one of its parts (the power meter of a machine) has a job or delivers the inputs: KPI coverage and potential count it once, for the asset. Off by default – a part’s data stands for the whole asset only where it measures all of it.

protocolOther.help: The base leaves the protocol open (“other”): choose the one this device speaks, then give its data points their addresses.
